prompt.context: Your client is Salt of the Earth Group, an Australian mining company with $40B in revenue. Salt of the Earth prides itself on mining and producing materials essential to drive economic progress and operates across 5 decentralized Product Groups: Iron Ore, Copper, Aluminum, Petroleum, and Coal. The company operates globally using a combination of wholly owned assets and Joint Ventures. Recently, commodities have experienced macro pressures: prices have fallen as global GDP underperforms, global demand for metals is plateauing as developing economies mature, and resources companies are having trouble attracting and retaining young talent. Despite this difficult environment, your client is a global leader and is committed to sustaining its competitive advantage. In its most recent earnings report, it promised shareholders an incremental $5B in cumulative net income over 5 years through a series of initiatives designed to unlock 'whole of system' value. Your team has been brought in to perform an analysis for the client's Executive Committee to identify whether $5B is even possible, and what will drive value.
prompt.question: Is the client's goal of $5B in cumulative net benefit over 5 years achievable, and what initiatives will drive that value?

clarifying_info.a: It is $5B in cumulative net benefit over a 5-year horizon, measured in USD. We are focused on the whole company, not a specific product group.

clarifying_info.q: What does 'whole of system' value mean?
clarifying_info.a: Delivering value across the entire value chain. Currently mining focuses on maximizing value for given nodes (e.g. the mine itself, processing, etc.) without connecting what happens in the mine to how and when the product is sold. This project seeks to make those connections.
The primary initiatives are investments in a 'way of working' (e.g. integrated org/process design) and an investment in cutting-edge IT.

clarifying_info.q: Can the company influence commodity prices?
clarifying_info.a: No. Price is dictated by the market and remains constant.

exhibits.title: Salt of the Earth Value Tree
exhibits.shows: A value tree mapping three value levers (Physical Product, Opex, Capex) to their full potential annual improvement percentages and the specific operational mechanisms driving each lever

data.Physical Product: +2.5% via Enhanced Planning, Improved Ore Recovery, Improved Throughput
data.Capex: -10% via Increased equipment life, Decreased Total Cost of Ownership

exhibits.title: Group Financial Statement
exhibits.shows: A simplified 2018 income statement for Salt of the Earth Group showing physical product volume, market price, revenue, opex, capex, earnings before taxes, taxes, and underlying earnings

data.Note: Price is market-dictated and constant; Underlying Earnings is used as performance metric

exhibits.title: Program Investment Profile
exhibits.shows: A year-by-year investment schedule from 2019 to 2023 broken out by IT project (Cloud Analytics, Autonomous Vehicles, Safety Geofencing, Machine Learning) and way-of-working initiatives (Org/Process Design, Change Strategy)

data.Projects: Cloud Analytics, Autonomous Vehicles, Safety Geofencing, Machine Learning, Transparent Op Model/Org and Process Design, Change Strategy and Implementation

exhibits.title: Value/Investment Ramp-Up
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing annual (not cumulative) value and investment figures from 2019 to 2023, illustrating how value ramps up while investment tapers down over the program horizon

data.Note: Figures represent value/investment delivered in year indicated; NOT cumulative

framework: Revenue (physical product): mining companies sell physical product — volume x price; price is market-dictated so focus is on volume/yield improvements
Opex (operating costs): labor, energy, maintenance — large lever given $25B base
Capex (capital expenditure): equipment life, total cost of ownership — capital-intensive industry
Investment required: achieving benefits requires upfront investment in IT and operating model; net benefit = gross benefit minus investment
Ramp-up timing: benefits unlikely to be realized in Year 1; need to model how quickly full potential is achieved
Non-financial value: talent attraction/retention, safety, environmental footprint (addressed in Prompt 2)

questions.prompt: Using Exhibits 1a and 1b, calculate the full potential annual incremental benefit to Underlying Earnings.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply each percentage improvement to the relevant financial line, flow through taxes at 40%, and arrive at $1.5B incremental Underlying Earnings per year at full potential.

math.setup: Apply value tree percentages from Exhibit 1a to the baseline financials in Exhibit 1b, then compute post-tax impact.
steps: Physical Product: 8,000,000 tons x +2.5% = +200,000 tons; Revenue uplift = 200,000 x $5,000 = +$1B incremental revenue
Incremental Underlying Earnings = $2.5B - $1B = $1.5B per year (full potential)
math.answer: $1.5B per year in incremental Underlying Earnings at full potential

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2b, calculate the total 5-year cumulative value, total 5-year investment, total 5-year net benefit, and ROI. Does the initiative meet the $5B goal?
questions.guidance: Candidate must recognize that Exhibit 2b figures are annual (not cumulative) and sum each column separately, then compute net benefit and ROI. Should note the client prefers ROI over NPV/IRR; time value of money can be ignored.

math.setup: Sum annual value and annual investment across 2019-2023 from Exhibit 2b, then compute Net Benefit = Value - Investment and ROI = (Benefit - Cost) / Cost.
steps: Conclusion: Yes, the initiative meets (and exceeds) the $5B cumulative net benefit goal.
math.answer: 5-Year Value: $6.2B; 5-Year Investment: $1B; 5-Year Net Benefit: $5.2B; ROI: 520%. The initiative meets the $5B goal.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond financials, the client wants the Executive Committee to be aware of the non-financial benefits that might be realized. What non-financial benefits do you want to highlight?

categories.name: Talent / Employee Engagement
ideas: Mining companies are having difficulty attracting and retaining young talent
Investing in cutting-edge IT (cloud analytics, autonomous vehicles, machine learning) creates a digital workforce
May improve ability to attract and retain younger employees who prefer tech-enabled environments

categories.name: Safety
ideas: Investment in Safety Geofencing (Exhibit 2a) creates a safer work environment
Reducing human exposure to hazardous conditions through autonomous vehicles

categories.name: Environmental
ideas: Operational transformation may reduce the client's operational footprint
Improved planning could reduce waste and energy consumption
May improve the client's ability to reclaim land that has been mined

recommendation: The transformation will deliver $5.2B in net value over a 5-year horizon, meeting and exceeding the $5B promise made to shareholders
Value will be delivered through increased physical product (+2.5%), reduced opex (-4%), and reduced capex (-10%), supported by a $1B investment primarily in cutting-edge IT
ROI is 520%, and non-financial benefits in talent, safety, and environment further strengthen the case
risks: Sensitivity of value to market commodity prices — a price decline would reduce the revenue uplift
Sufficient market demand for incremental product volume — 200,000 additional tons must be absorbed
Capabilities and culture required to deliver a large-scale IT transformation of this nature
Labor union resistance to automation (autonomous vehicles, machine learning) and workforce changes
next_steps: Align investment with value and prioritize highest-ROI initiatives within the program
Align internal capabilities and form a dedicated program team
Secure external support for the IT transformation
Develop change management strategy to address culture and union concerns
